cards.explanation: The answer is bound on his heart and tied around his neck. The teacher says, "Bind them always upon your heart; tie them around your neck." Heart AND neck. That's not a sticky note on the fridge, friends, that's wearing the thing. I can lose a recipe card in my own apron pocket, so I respect this level of closeness.

The answer is True. The teacher says, "when you lie down, they will watch over you…" So even when the son lies down, the teaching is still on the job. Some folks can't even keep an eye on the clock while they're awake, friends, so that's impressive.

The answer is life. The teacher says "…the reproofs of discipline are the way to life…" (Proverbs 6:23). Correction can sting a little, friends, but it points the right way. Right next to the lamp and the light, it keeps the son walking toward life.

The answer is the evil woman with a smooth tongue. The teaching is there "…to keep you from the evil woman, from the smooth tongue of the adulteress." Notice it's her smooth tongue that gets the warning, friends.

The answer is False. The teacher says, "Do not lust in your heart for her beauty…" That's a warning about the heart, not just about what the son does. He's talking about what the son wants inside before anything shows on the outside, friends.

The answer is her beauty and her eyes. The teacher says, "Do not lust in your heart for her beauty or let her captivate you with her eyes." Beauty and eyes, those are the two. Eyes are tricky, friends. I once stared at one cookie for ten minutes and forgot the rest of the batch.

The answer is True. The teacher says, "…the adulteress preys upon your very life." Your very life, bakers, not just your pocket. He's not whispering a small warning here. He's telling the son how much is at stake.

The answer is False. The teacher asks, "Can a man embrace fire and his clothes not be burned?" He's asking something everybody already knows. Hold fire close and you get burned, friends. Nobody needs a long lecture about it.

The answer is True. The teacher says, "no one who touches her will go unpunished." He's talking about the man who sleeps with another man's wife. After the fire and the hot coals, friends, this is where he lands.

The answer is that he must pay back sevenfold. The teacher says, "Yet if caught, he must pay sevenfold…" And that's for a thief who stole because he was hungry. So if even that thief pays a heavy price, friends, you can see where the teacher is going with the adulterer.

The answers are judgment and himself. The teacher says, "He who commits adultery lacks judgment…" He's saying the man isn't thinking clearly. Then he says, "whoever does so destroys himself." Not a stranger, not a rival. The damage lands on the man himself. That's a heavy line, friends.
The answer is jealousy. The teacher says, "For jealousy enrages a husband…" Jealousy is the word he picks, friends. He also says the husband "…will show no mercy in the day of vengeance."

The answer is False. The teacher says, "He will not be appeased by any ransom, or persuaded by lavish gifts." So no amount of gifts settles things in the day of vengeance. He's showing how serious it is, friends.
